A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the standard SI/ SD treatment is a special case of a general treatment that includes derivative interactions and that the standard treatment misses important effects in the case of derivative interactions.
the SI/SD formulation is not a good approximation to the full model-independent analysis, and that the latter must be used to properly analyze current data and plan future experiments.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard SI/ SD treatment of WIMP scattering, while adequate for many purposes, is insufficient for model-independent analyses.

, in the absence of any model assumptions about the underlying particle physics, the standard SI/ SD treatment of dark matter-nucleon scattering is not only incomplete, but it can be dangerously misleading.
